$comment: ``CandidateDispositionLog.v1`` -- an APPEND-ONLY history of what became of
each recorded candidate artifact. Owner and checker:
`scripts/foundation_disposition.py`. Gate:
`tests/architecture/test_foundation_candidate_disposition.py`.
## Why this file is not a field on the candidate receipt
`CandidateArtifact.v1` records bytes that were built once. That record
cannot become false -- only the candidate's USABILITY can -- and a
restore proof, an issuer stand-up and a Lane 3 rehearsal all bind to the
receipt. A receipt editable after those bindings exist is a receipt whose
meaning changes underneath them. So the receipt is frozen and every later
judgement is appended here, bound to it by digest.
## How append-only is PROVED rather than promised
1. Hash chain. Entry n>1 carries the canonical digest of entry n-1, so
editing any historical entry invalidates every entry after it.
2. The anchor. Entry 1 chains to the digest of the receipt it
dispositions, not to a zero genesis -- so the same check proves the
log was not rewritten AND that CandidateArtifact.v1 was not touched.
3. A two-directional count ratchet (ADR-0018): EXPECTED_ENTRIES fails on
growth as well as on shrinkage, so an append is legitimate and cannot
be silent.
Editing an entry in place is not a supported operation. A judgement that
turned out wrong is corrected by appending the correction, because a log
that can be edited is not evidence of anything.
## A disposition authorizes nothing
`publishable: false` records a fact. The REFUSAL that acts on it lives in
the version-binding guard, which reads this log. A record that both
states a fact and enforces it is one edit away from being neither.
